overview: This file assembles American diplomatic and intelligence reporting on Japanese military preparations in Taiwan from late 1941 through 1943. It begins with a consular telegram describing conspicuous troop concentrations and exercises around Taipei and across central and southern Taiwan, followed by an FBI report on the fortification of southern Taiwan, the expansion of Kaohsiung harbor, civil-defense preparations, and Japanese efforts to mobilize and indoctrinate Taiwanese and Koreans. The later documents transmit unverified intelligence supplied in Chongqing by Taiwanese associated with the Taiwan Revolutionary League, covering Japanese expectations of a direct American attack, defenses and naval bases, conscription and declining agricultural production, and the locations, garrisons, and aircraft complements of Taiwanese airfields.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese troop concentrations and exercises in Taiwan
subfiles.from: Bruner at Taihoku, forwarded by Joseph C. Grew at Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports unusually large Japanese troop concentrations, billeting, training, and military displays in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Bruner reports troops quartered in Taipei schools and across Taiwan, describing field telephones, exercises, artillery, tanks, machine guns, and aircraft maneuvers, plus thousands making an organized pilgrimage to Taiwan's main shrine.

subfiles.title: Hoskins note concerning the Koreans
subfiles.about: Briefly urges that something be done concerning the Koreans.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten note says action should be taken on the Koreans, linked to later discussion of military indoctrination in Korea/Taiwan.

subfiles.title: Berle memorandum recommending circulation of the December 11 report
subfiles.about: Recommends distributing the December 11 memorandum to senior American intelligence and military authorities.
subfiles.summary: Berle calls the December 11 report highly significant, recommending it circulate to the Coordinator of Information and the War and Navy Secretaries.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on Japanese indoctrination of Koreans and Taiwanese
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs; drafted by Salisbury
subfiles.about: Highlights the FBI report's warning that Japanese military nationalism had influenced young Koreans and Taiwanese.
subfiles.summary: Memo argues Japanese education and military ideology conditioned Koreans and Taiwanese toward nationalism, warning the younger generation could become a powerful instrument unless discredited quickly.

subfiles.title: Hoover letter forwarding intelligence on South Formosa
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr.; copy to Captain T. S. Wilkinson
subfiles.about: Forwards confidential-source information about the Province of Takao in southern Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends Berle confidential FBI intelligence on South Formosa's Takao Province, also copied to Naval Intelligence.

subfiles.title: FBI memorandum on military preparations and political conditioning in Taiwan
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation, based on an outside confidential source
subfiles.about: Describes southern Taiwan's militarization, air-defense preparations, and the ideological mobilization of Taiwanese and Koreans.
subfiles.summary: FBI memo: southern Taiwan was closed to foreigners, fortified, and garrisoned, with Kaohsiung harbor improved and transports at Penghu; it also claims Japanese schooling deeply shaped young Taiwanese/Korean nationalism, advancing sweeping, prejudicial racial-loyalty claims.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum summarizing the Chungking despatch
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs; drafted by Max W. Bishop
subfiles.about: Summarizes intelligence on Japanese preparations for a possible American attack on Taiwan and on Taiwanese airfields.
subfiles.summary: Memo reviews a Chungking despatch's intelligence on expected American attack on Taiwan and Japanese countermeasures, noting the airfield report reached Stilwell's headquarters.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 134 transmitting information concerning Formosa
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Chungking
subfiles.about: Transmits two translated reports obtained from Taiwanese connected with the Taiwan Revolutionary League.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson forwards unverified reports that Japan expected direct American attack on Taiwan, with conscription, land seizure, and cattle slaughter reducing production.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 1: Increasing Significance of Formosa in International Problems
subfiles.from: Research Office identified as (金山), through Formosa News No. 223
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese preparations against a direct American attack and the military and economic effects of mobilization in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure claims Japan strengthened Taiwan's defenses after Attu's recapture and nearby submarine attacks, planting trees for cover and roads, while conscripting 280,000-plus men and seizing farmland, cutting production 20-30 percent.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 2: Further Establishments of Air Force Bases in Formosa
subfiles.from: Research Office identified as (合二), through News from Formosa No. 224
subfiles.about: Inventories Japanese civil, army, and naval airfields in Taiwan and supplies estimates of their troops and aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure identifies Taiwan air bases at Taichung, Tainan, Songshan, Taoyuan, Chiayi, Gangshan, and Pingtung, with construction dates, units, and aircraft counts; an eighth field at Hualien was being expedited for future Pacific operations.

interest: Shows layered U.S. intelligence on Taiwan's wartime militarization, from field reports to FBI data and racial assumptions.
